Use Cases

eve's two most common use cases are business agents for your own company and agents you ship to customers as a product.

For your team Business agents

Automate a company function, like analytics, a software factory, marketing, or finance.

  • Slack
  • Microsoft Teams
  • GitHub
  • Linear
  • Web
For your customers Agent as a Service (AaaS)

Build multi-tenant agentic applications that scale as you grow.

  • iMessage
  • WhatsApp
  • Telegram
  • Discord
  • Web

Business agents

A business agent takes on work for teams inside your company. Employees reach the agent in Slack, Microsoft Teams, or GitHub, and it acts on the company's own systems and data.

Software factory

Agents plan features, open pull requests, review code, and respond to incidents alongside an engineering team.

Software Factory template Company brain

One agent holds the company's skills, tools, and approved connections, reachable where employees work.

Company Brain template Marketing team

A lead agent routes work to specialists for positioning, long-form content, social, SEO, and email, then publishes through Notion, Typefully, and Resend.

Marketing team template

How eve supports business agents

An eve agent lives in your repository, so it is reviewed, deployed, and governed like the rest of your stack.

  • Meet employees where they work

    One agent serves Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, Linear, and your own web apps, with a session for every conversation.

    Channels
  • Govern and audit every run

    OpenTelemetry traces and Agent Runs record every session, model call, and tool call, so you can see what an agent did and why.

    Observability
  • Use your identity provider

    Verify callers with any OIDC issuer, JWTs, or your own authenticator. Each connection then acts as the agent itself or on behalf of the signed-in user.

    Identity and access
  • Switch models without a code rewrite

    Changing models is a one-line edit in agent.ts, and requests can fall back to another provider on failure.

    Models
  • Connect to approved services

    Expose the MCP and OpenAPI services your IT team approves. Credentials stay in the runtime, and the model never sees them.

    Connections
  • Evaluate agent responses

    Evals run the agent through real turns and score the result with code checks or a model judge.

    Evals
  • Put deterministic steps in the loop

    Tools are typed TypeScript functions the model chooses when to call. When a process must run the same way every time, use a workflow tool instead.

    Workflow tools
  • Run commands in sandboxed compute

    Each session gets an isolated filesystem and shell for scripts, repositories, and generated files.

    Sandbox
  • Keep a human in the loop

    Sessions pause while an approval is pending and resume when it resolves, even after a redeploy.

    Human-in-the-loop

Agent as a Service (AaaS)

In AaaS, the agent is the product. One multi-tenant deployment serves many customers over long stretches of time.

Start building

Create an agent and open the terminal UI.

npx eve@latest init my-agent
